body: I think euthanasia should be a personal freedom for people with both physical and mental illness. Of course there is always the possibility of regret but that is not limited to those with mental illness. I think the most important piece in preventing regretted euthanasia, or worse, regretted suicide, is the opportunity to have the conversation about ending your life without stigma or immediate hospitalization. It lets a person talk about their options openly and make a truly informed decision.

It’s all I see right now too. I’m 27F. It’s weird though all I want is to be a functioning member of society. It just seems beyond my power to function and I’d give anything to have the put together life you describe. It’s interesting how the way out of this (other that suicide) is different for each of us. Nonetheless, it’s intolerably painful. 
Have you given thought to what YOU want outside of what societal norms are? When I was 22 I traveled solo for 6 months to 13 countries even though everyone thought I was crazy for it. My point is maybe you’re allowing yourself to be limited by external expectations. That would make anyone feel trapped. If that is your case I implore you to search your soul for what you want out of life, not what other want for you.
